title: RFI, grounding and bonding
blurb: Explain how RF gets into audio equipment, what each sound means, and why ground wires and bonding matter.

G4C01.why: A **bypass capacitor** passes RF to ground but blocks the audio, so it removes RF from audio circuits.
G4C01.trap: A shunt inductor does the reverse: it passes audio to ground and resists RF.

G4C02.why: Sparks from an **arc** at a poor connection are made of all frequencies, so the noise is broad.
G4C02.trap: Baluns and rectification affect specific paths, not wide spectra.

G4C03.why: SSB is a changing voice envelope with no steady carrier, so the victim detects **distorted speech**.
G4C03.trap: Humming or clicking is what a keyed CW carrier sounds like.

G4C04.why: CW keys the carrier on and off, so the victim hears **on-and-off humming or clicking** with each element.
G4C04.trap: A pure tone or speech is not what an unwanted keyed carrier sounds like.

G4C05.why: A ground wire with **high impedance at your frequency** lets RF voltage build on connected metal, which can burn you.
G4C05.trap: Flat versus round or insulated wire isn't the issue. Impedance at your frequency is.

G4C06.why: A resonant ground presents high impedance at the equipment, so **high RF voltage** appears on enclosures.
G4C06.trap: That is an RF effect, not corrosion or a ground loop.

G4C07.why: A lightning strike's heat can melt solder, so soldered joints are likely to be **destroyed by the heat**.

G4C08.why: Common-mode RF on a cable is stopped by a **ferrite choke** on the cable, which presents high impedance to RF.
G4C08.trap: Shorting or grounding the center conductor shorts the audio itself.

G4C09.why: Loops form between separately grounded equipment. **Bonding enclosures together** keeps them at one potential.
G4C09.trap: Series connections and neutral-to-ground ties don't remove loops.

G4C10.why: A ground loop injects current into audio paths, which shows up as **hum on your transmitted signal**.
G4C10.trap: SWR, current draw and harmonics are not ground-loop symptoms.

G4C11.why: RF hot spots are voltage differences between enclosures. **Bonding all enclosures together** removes them.
G4C11.trap: Filters and surge suppressors don't equalize enclosure voltages.

G4C12.why: A grounded enclosure keeps a fault from putting **hazardous voltage on the chassis**, where you could touch it.
G4C12.trap: Grounding is about shock safety, not fuses or overload.
